articleTitle: An engineering approach to control design and analysis for flexible aircraft
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrating Control System Design with the Analysis of Flexible Structures
abstract: The objectives of this research at the Royal Aerospace Establishment, Farnborough, were the improvement of aeroelastic modelling techniques, the development of design methods for active control technology (ACT), and the assessment of the impact of ACT on aircraft structures. Related experimental have included the measurements of aircraft responses in flight on VC10 and tornado aircraft, and experiments to demonstrate the implementation of control system on wind tunnel models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modal reduction guided by Hankel singular value intervals (with application to control design for compact disc players)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrating Control System Design with the Analysis of Flexible Structures
abstract: A simple procedure is proposed to find sets of modes that are input-output dominant. Hankel singular value intervals are derived that estimate the reachability-observability of sets of modes. Eigenvalue perturbation theory of Gersgorin is used to determine these intervals and to check that the reachability and observability Gramians of the modal realization approximate the diagonal Gramians of an internally balanced realization. The application of the technique to compact disc mechanism control design is briefly described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Control structures interaction on actively controlled aircraft
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrating Control System Design with the Analysis of Flexible Structures
abstract: High performance fighter aircraft with high gain control systems often have multiple closely coupled structural modes which can interact unfavourably with their feedback control systems. The paper describes the analysis of control structures interaction and illustrates the use of notch filters to eliminate it by way of a simple example. It goes on to describe possible alternative approaches to assisting the problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: mu -synthesis application to flexible structures: a review of the work of Balas
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrating Control System Design with the Analysis of Flexible Structures
abstract: Advances in the control of flexible structures are necessitated by the stringent requirements on pointing and shape accuracy of some future space mission. The author reviews the work of Balas in the application of mu methods to an experimental structure. A discussion of mu methods is provided and the important area of uncertainty descriptions is covered. The mu -synthesis method has the advantage that it can take the structure of these uncertainties into account during design. The results of the mu -synthesis designs are discussed, and conclusions are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
